references.text: Abram traveled through the land to the place near Shechem, to the oak of Moreh. This is the same grove at Moreh mentioned in Deuteronomy 11:30.
Jacob buried the idols under the terebinth tree near Shechem, close to the same area where the oaks of Moreh were located.
Gilgal is mentioned as the place where the Israelites camped after crossing the Jordan, corresponding to 'across from Gilgal' in this text.
Gilgal was the first stopping place for the Israelites west of the Jordan and is the reference point mentioned in this verse.
Joshua set up a stone under the oak tree at the Lord's sanctuary in Shechem, which is near the oaks of Moreh.
Mentions the oak by the pillar at Shechem, which is in the same area as the oaks of Moreh.
Refers to the 'Prophet's Oak,' which is likely the same grove at Moreh.
Describes Israel in the Arabah (the wilderness/plain), the same area mentioned in this verse.
